before.title: Autodesk funded development and acceptance
before.description: Autodesk funded development and acceptance Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

inputs.description: Native AIONix/ERA build with reliable floating-point geometry and typed coordinate entry
Dual-display driver with colour command/status screen and 800x600 drawing canvas; independent palettes and explicit input focus
Explicit CAD mouse integration; standard TUI mouse support alone is insufficient
Drawing load/save and DXF exchange tests against the other supported AutoCAD builds
Supported pen-plotter output and physical drawing verification
Measured RAM, storage, redraw and stability requirements on the qualified configuration; backup/restore and reproducible release build
Feature baseline agreed with Autodesk; no automatic import of later AutoCAD dimensioning, object-snap or 3D features

team environment / workstations: Supply an Artemis PRO with 1 MiB RAM, local storage and available display to each assigned developer, plus shared build/test and spare machines as the agreed staffing plan requires. No invented fixed team size.

team environment / software: Install the entire AION Development System — Team Edition: C Development Environment 2, ERA compiler/linker/debugger and validated floating-point math library; source repository, branches/reviews, tasks, collaboration, reproducible builds, release labels and target testing.

team environment / network: Supply network adapters, hub, cabling, configured accounts and project permissions, and dedicated Artemis PRO server capacity. Scale sponsored server/license deployments to the whole team within qualified concurrency; the retail four-session entitlement is not silently unlimited.

team environment / storage: The standard 5 MB disk is inadequate as a presumed whole-team repository/build archive. Fund and qualify larger storage, additional volumes/servers, independent backup media, restore tests and off-machine source archives; capacities follow measured source/build/history budgets.

team environment / support: Fund dedicated Autodesk engineering time, AION compiler/runtime and integration specialists, installation, training, documentation, replacement hardware, plotter access and on-site support through release. Retail onboarding/support-hour caps do not limit this separately sponsored agreement.

team environment / early graphics: January work uses available Artemis PRO displays and a stable software implementation of the graphics API. Supply 64 KiB/Color Pro engineering samples and mouse prototypes when qualified; do not make January work depend on the June professional hardware.

team environment / professional handover: Around June 1982 deliver the 128 KiB professional card and Logix Mono Pro 17 to the development and QA team, alongside the 64 KiB colour card/Color Pro 14 and mouse. This supersedes the earlier proposed January 17-inch prototype handover.

funding: Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective.

outcomes.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

professional hardware revision: COMDEX November revision adds explicit inherited modes, palette sequencing and five-sprite compatibility; preserve June development handover. See dated revisions in the catalog.

steps.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.
Meet programme acceptance gates; commercial shipment remains conditional on acceptance.

before.title: Frankfurt stay, lottery win and preparation for New York
before.description: Adam stays in an apartment at the Leonardo Royal Hotel Frankfurt until his departure for New York. During the stay he wins LOTTO 6aus49 using foreknowledge and transfers the proceeds to his New York bank account.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: Adam’s permanent departure from Birmingham and arrival in Frankfurt establish this temporary stay.
Adam has money and remaining belongings from Birmingham, accommodation in Frankfurt, and knowledge of the lottery result.

steps.description: Stay in the Frankfurt hotel apartment until departure.
Enter LOTTO 6aus49 and match six winning numbers.
Collect the winnings and send the proceeds to the First National City Bank account in New York.
Leave Frankfurt by air for New York.

outcomes.description: The Frankfurt stay is complete and Adam departs for New York.
Lottery proceeds have been sent to Adam’s account at First National City Bank in New York.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy — execution
before.description: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.

outcomes.description: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage

steps.description: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.
Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal.
NCC premiere in Anaheim, five-city Academy announcement, package and availability presentation, registration and ordering.
Technical sessions, repeated hands-on demonstrations, professional recording of every Logix NCC presentation and Academy registration.

Edit and freely distribute television packages; run Academy courses and dealer demonstrations; advertise practical business uses, real package prices, local dates and documented customer experience as it becomes available.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.
broadcast program / scope: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions.

broadcast program / production: Professional multi-camera crew with clean presenter audio, audience/reaction coverage and close-ups of the computer, screen, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

broadcast program / distribution: Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.
broadcast program / broadcast fee usd: 0

broadcast program / editorial policy: Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary; no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or claimed editorial endorsement. Identify the material as supplied by Logix.

broadcast program / rights: Arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights covering free television redistribution before recording. Michael Douglas commercial footage may be included only if separately cleared for this use.

broadcast program / fidelity: Do not accelerate startup or recalculation, conceal failures through misleading cuts, or present pre-recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and show only qualified claims.

broadcast program / timing: Record throughout June 5–8; begin station outreach before NCC and distribute edited packages after the conference as edits and broadcast clearances are completed. Exact delivery dates and runtime remain production decisions.

broadcast program / engineering: Qualify a custom Aurelia digital-video-to-projection/recording path; rehearse readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Use a backup demonstration system and clearly identified recorded fallback.
Post-NCC 1978 recording, editing and television distribution

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign — execution
before.description: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral manufacturers to the published compatibility programmes, and help existing customers carry their applications and documents across supported systems.

steps.description: Begin confidential briefings and engineering-kit evaluations. Prioritise North Star and Vector Graphic as prospects; approach Cromemco, Altos, Intertec and Heath selectively. Invitations are not signed agreements or qualified products.

Alongside the existing DRI portable-extension release, publish separate CP/M application, FlexiBUS peripheral and optional Logix display compatibility profiles, reference-driver and test access, non-exclusive implementation principles and support-roadmap requirements. Exact fees and support duration remain to be settled.

Invite computer, software and peripheral suppliers to test named configurations and document failures before public demonstrations. Supplier attendance and passing results must be verified; no announcement of an unsigned OEM.

Present a 50-minute cross-vendor campaign before questions. Demonstrate applications/documents, then independent BPI, FlexiBUS, Apple native drivers and optional video. BPI management speaks with partners. State that the next generation breaks native Z80 binary compatibility; C source/API portability reduces migration work and a planned optional Z80 compatibility coprocessor supports qualified legacy software. Reveal neither processor word size nor architecture before NCC 1980. See ncc_1979_campaign.json.

Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Teach documented APIs, file interchange, C portability boundaries and device-class drivers. Publish a directory distinguishing shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.

Promote the separately recorded Tandy customer release and only individually qualified SMC or peripheral products. Update directory evidence; do not imply all licensed chips, every peripheral class or new independent OEM systems are shipping.

Target Tandy shipping, one additional named OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension/FlexiBUS option, another OEM in qualification, dealer/integrator configurations and third-party devices in several categories. These are adoption targets, not recorded achievements or contracted orders.

Publish verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Target three to five non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations by NCC 1980, counting Tandy once and excluding duplicate dealer builds. Do not disclose the new processor architecture early.
existing anchors / Tandy: Existing agreement: CP/M, native display adapter, FlexiBUS option and Abacus; no video requirement or BPI port.
existing anchors / Apple: Existing native expansion cooperation and peripheral/display demonstrations; no Z80 or CP/M execution provided.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy — execution
before.description: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.

outcomes.description: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage

steps.description: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.
Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal.
NCC premiere in Anaheim, five-city Academy announcement, package and availability presentation, registration and ordering.
Technical sessions, repeated hands-on demonstrations, professional recording of every Logix NCC presentation and Academy registration.

Edit and freely distribute television packages; run Academy courses and dealer demonstrations; advertise practical business uses, real package prices, local dates and documented customer experience as it becomes available.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.
broadcast program / scope: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions.

broadcast program / production: Professional multi-camera crew with clean presenter audio, audience/reaction coverage and close-ups of the computer, screen, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

broadcast program / distribution: Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.
broadcast program / broadcast fee usd: 0

broadcast program / editorial policy: Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary; no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or claimed editorial endorsement. Identify the material as supplied by Logix.

broadcast program / rights: Arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights covering free television redistribution before recording. Michael Douglas commercial footage may be included only if separately cleared for this use.

broadcast program / fidelity: Do not accelerate startup or recalculation, conceal failures through misleading cuts, or present pre-recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and show only qualified claims.

broadcast program / timing: Record throughout June 5–8; begin station outreach before NCC and distribute edited packages after the conference as edits and broadcast clearances are completed. Exact delivery dates and runtime remain production decisions.

broadcast program / engineering: Qualify a custom Aurelia digital-video-to-projection/recording path; rehearse readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Use a backup demonstration system and clearly identified recorded fallback.
Post-NCC 1978 recording, editing and television distribution

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy — execution
before.description: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.

outcomes.description: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage

steps.description: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.
Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal.
NCC premiere in Anaheim, five-city Academy announcement, package and availability presentation, registration and ordering.
Technical sessions, repeated hands-on demonstrations, professional recording of every Logix NCC presentation and Academy registration.

Edit and freely distribute television packages; run Academy courses and dealer demonstrations; advertise practical business uses, real package prices, local dates and documented customer experience as it becomes available.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

Logix supplies Aurelia platform requirements, interface knowledge and integration work; DRI develops and integrates the CP/M operating-system changes. They cooperate on interoperability and qualification for Aurelia. Hardware, devices and cards remain platform deliverables rather than DRI hardware-manufacturing obligations.

DRI fully owns the new CP/M version and its CP/M software enhancements developed through this collaboration. DRI may offer and license that version to any other vendor on non-exclusive terms. Aurelia compatibility and Logix collaboration confer no exclusive CP/M distribution right on Logix. Hardware and technology ownership are not transferred by this software-ownership term.

Provide a text-mode TUI: pseudo-window interfaces, menus and shared interaction conventions that make applications usable through a consistent text-screen interface. Integrate the Logix TUI standard with CP/M software services.
Support smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute and FlexiBUS technologies, with documented CP/M integration so qualified devices and cards can expose their functions to applications.
Support XIP cartridges and their software interfaces so suitable programs can execute in place from cartridge ROM on compatible hardware.

Allow names to be assigned to CP/M file User Numbers, presenting user areas as named directory-like locations. This supplies a named organisation layer over User Numbers without asserting a new hierarchical filesystem.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
before.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

positioning / partner message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
claim_policy: Legacy acceptance wording (not new confirmation) / status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

acceptance gates / 0: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
acceptance gates / 1: Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
acceptance gates / 2: Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, tuition, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified and separately quoted.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

broadcast policy: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The following BPI demonstration shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

stage.label: bpi
stage.description: Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in the subsequent partners section.

stage.label: partners
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: academy
stage.description: Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice, 50% tuition purchase credit and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates and exact tuition once finalised. BPI-authorised courses start June 12; specialist support is provided by BPI.

stage.label: packages
stage.description: State complete package contents and prices, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training/setup prices.

stage.label: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem
stage.description: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

stage.label: Aurelia C compiler Integrated Development Environment and SDK
stage.description: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

stage.label: premiere / venue
stage.description: Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.

stage.label: premiere / stages / 7 / description
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with AION/Logix cooperation and Adam’s uncompleted investment offer disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: premiere / questions
stage.description: Moderated questions follow the presentation.

stage.label: premiere / display
stage.description: Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

stage.label: technical sessions / 0 / topic
stage.description: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem

stage.label: technical sessions / 1 / topic
stage.description: Aurelia C compiler Integrated Development Environment and SDK

stage.label: business sessions / 0 / provider
stage.description: BPI Systems

stage.label: business sessions / 0 / topic
stage.description: Setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage

marketing_content.description: Proposed 60-second film-trailer-style advertisement; final 10–15 seconds show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, logo and June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable BPI report with its own branding; detailed accounting explanation belongs in print and follow-up films.
Michael Douglas

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration.
Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence.
Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.
A modest fraction of an Aurelia package price; publish exact tuition and a named package comparison when commercial prices are selected. Generated pricing proposals are not approved tuition.
Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases.
Aurelia Fundamentals
Academy direct sales
participating authorised dealers
Logix reimburses participating dealers; do not deduct the credit from their agreed margin.
false
Standalone two-day Fundamentals. Existing $150 vouchers for the other before-you-buy courses remain unchanged; no stacking or extension to other courses is implied.
Reserve the redeemed credit once as promotional expense across the course and computer sale, outside recurring manufacturing costs.
Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.

Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate; no automatic Fundamentals credit for BPI courses.

party.role: Aurelia platform partner and development collaborator
CP/M developer, sole software owner and licensor
negotiator for the Logix collaboration

before.description: Logix and Digital Research agree to develop a new CP/M version for Logix Aurelia. DRI fully owns the resulting CP/M version and makes it available to other vendors through non-exclusive licensing. The collaboration adds a text-mode TUI, smart-device and card integration, XIP cartridge support and named user areas.

clauses.statement: DRI retains the right to implement the TUI libraries and FlexiBUS support in CP/M versions for non-Logix computers.

Logix supplies Aurelia platform requirements, interface knowledge and integration work; DRI develops and integrates the CP/M operating-system changes. They cooperate on interoperability and qualification for Aurelia. Hardware, devices and cards remain platform deliverables rather than DRI hardware-manufacturing obligations.

DRI fully owns the new CP/M version and its CP/M software enhancements developed through this collaboration. DRI may offer and license that version to any other vendor on non-exclusive terms. Aurelia compatibility and Logix collaboration confer no exclusive CP/M distribution right on Logix. Hardware and technology ownership are not transferred by this software-ownership term.

Provide a text-mode TUI: pseudo-window interfaces, menus and shared interaction conventions that make applications usable through a consistent text-screen interface. Integrate the Logix TUI standard with CP/M software services.
Support smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute and FlexiBUS technologies, with documented CP/M integration so qualified devices and cards can expose their functions to applications.
Support XIP cartridges and their software interfaces so suitable programs can execute in place from cartridge ROM on compatible hardware.

Allow names to be assigned to CP/M file User Numbers, presenting user areas as named directory-like locations. This supplies a named organisation layer over User Numbers without asserting a new hierarchical filesystem.

Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective.

Autodesk undertook to deliver a release-quality Artemis/AIONix build of AutoCAD 1.0 for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation. Commercial deliveries followed acceptance of the agreed drawing, exchange, plotting and recovery tests.

Supply an Artemis PRO with 1 MiB RAM, local storage and available display to each assigned developer, plus shared build/test and spare machines as the agreed staffing plan requires. No invented fixed team size.

Install the entire AION Development System — Team Edition: C Development Environment 2, ERA compiler/linker/debugger and validated floating-point math library; source repository, branches/reviews, tasks, collaboration, reproducible builds, release labels and target testing.

Supply network adapters, hub, cabling, configured accounts and project permissions, and dedicated Artemis PRO server capacity. Scale sponsored server/license deployments to the whole team within qualified concurrency; the retail four-session entitlement is not silently unlimited.

The standard 5 MB disk is inadequate as a presumed whole-team repository/build archive. Fund and qualify larger storage, additional volumes/servers, independent backup media, restore tests and off-machine source archives; capacities follow measured source/build/history budgets.

Explicit CAD mouse integration; standard TUI mouse support alone is insufficient
Drawing load/save and DXF exchange tests against the other supported AutoCAD builds
Supported pen-plotter output and physical drawing verification
Measured RAM, storage, redraw and stability requirements on the qualified configuration; backup/restore and reproducible release build
Feature baseline agreed with Autodesk; no automatic import of later AutoCAD dimensioning, object-snap or 3D features

before.title: Logix and DRI agree CP/M development for Aurelia
before.description: Building on the established DRI partnership, Logix and DRI agree a new CP/M version for Aurelia, fully owned by DRI and available to other vendors. Its development scope includes a text-mode TUI, Plug and Execute smart devices/cards over FlexiBUS, XIP cartridges and names for CP/M User Numbers.

inputs.description: The earlier DRI founding and funding milestone establishes the independent operating-system partner and relationship on which this CP/M collaboration is based.

outcomes.description: The agreed product is a new CP/M version for Logix Aurelia, fully owned by DRI and available for non-exclusive licensing to other vendors. Its scope includes XIP cartridges and named CP/M user areas; implementation and qualification follow this agreement.
The agreement establishes integration of the Logix TUI standard into the CP/M development scope: a consistent pseudo-window user interface in text mode for participating applications.

The agreement establishes CP/M integration work for FlexiBUS smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute. This outcome covers agreed software support, not invention or completed manufacture of the underlying bus.

outcomes.description: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage

steps.description: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.
Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal.
NCC premiere in Anaheim, five-city Academy announcement, package and availability presentation, registration and ordering.
Technical sessions, repeated hands-on demonstrations, professional recording of every Logix NCC presentation and Academy registration.

Edit and freely distribute television packages; run Academy courses and dealer demonstrations; advertise practical business uses, real package prices, local dates and documented customer experience as it becomes available.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.
broadcast program / scope: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions.

broadcast program / production: Professional multi-camera crew with clean presenter audio, audience/reaction coverage and close-ups of the computer, screen, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

broadcast program / distribution: Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.
broadcast program / broadcast fee usd: 0

broadcast program / editorial policy: Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary; no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or claimed editorial endorsement. Identify the material as supplied by Logix.

broadcast program / rights: Arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights covering free television redistribution before recording. Michael Douglas commercial footage may be included only if separately cleared for this use.

broadcast program / fidelity: Do not accelerate startup or recalculation, conceal failures through misleading cuts, or present pre-recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and show only qualified claims.

broadcast program / timing: Record throughout June 5–8; begin station outreach before NCC and distribute edited packages after the conference as edits and broadcast clearances are completed. Exact delivery dates and runtime remain production decisions.

broadcast program / engineering: Qualify a custom Aurelia digital-video-to-projection/recording path; rehearse readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Use a backup demonstration system and clearly identified recorded fallback.
Post-NCC 1978 recording, editing and television distribution

before.title: BPI investment, C/TUI redevelopment and future-platform agreement

party.role: investor receiving a 33% fully diluted interest
accepting company and software owner
committed redevelopment and porting partner

before.description: BPI Systems accepts Adam’s $150,000 investment in exchange for a 33% fully diluted interest. The agreement obliges AION Software to provide knowledge and resources to refactor BPI’s existing code into C with a competitive text-mode TUI. Further investment supports ports to future systems and platforms, after which BPI has the right to buy back Adam’s shares.

clauses.statement: Adam agrees to subscribe $150,000 of new capital into BPI Systems for development and working capital. BPI accepts the subscription; it is company funding rather than a payment to existing owners.

The accepted investment agreement allocates Adam a 33% fully diluted interest in BPI Systems in exchange for his $150,000 subscription. Existing owners retain the remaining 67%, subject to the agreed later buyback right.
clauses.unit: percent of BPI fully diluted shares

clauses.statement: AION Software must provide the knowledge, engineering resources and development assistance needed to refactor BPI’s current code into C and deliver a competitive TUI with pseudo-window interaction in text mode. BPI retains ownership of its applications and its independent brand and management.

The cooperation includes further investment and engineering work to port the refactored BPI software to future systems and platforms. AION Software supplies the associated technical knowledge and resources. Additional funding amounts, allocation among contributors, target platforms and schedules remain unspecified.

Following the agreed redevelopment and subsequent porting work, BPI Systems may buy back Adam’s shares. This is BPI’s right, not an automatic transfer or a mandatory buyback. The agreement does not specify a price, valuation formula, exercise date or payment schedule.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy — execution
before.description: Starting on 26 March 1978, the day after the Logix Computer Academy is established, Logix coordinates the Aurelia launch campaign, qualified demonstrations, NCC presentations, BPI training and dealer follow-up through the customer-results and expansion milestone on 15 January 1979.

inputs.description: The Academy’s establishment on 25 March provides the training organisation and preparation basis for the campaign that begins the next day.

outcomes.description: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage
The campaign has presented Aurelia and independent BPI applications, opened Academy BPI training and supported dealer follow-up through the customer-results and expansion milestone.

steps.description: Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Coordinate the teaser, advertising, press and dealer preparation, then the nested NCC launch, technical sessions and media activities.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.
Begin Academy-authorised practical BPI courses and direct distribution on 12 June 1978, with distinct training, licensing and support responsibilities.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.
broadcast program / scope: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions.

broadcast program / production: Professional multi-camera crew with clean presenter audio, audience/reaction coverage and close-ups of the computer, screen, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

broadcast program / distribution: Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.
broadcast program / broadcast fee usd: 0

broadcast program / editorial policy: Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary; no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or claimed editorial endorsement. Identify the material as supplied by Logix.

broadcast program / rights: Arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights covering free television redistribution before recording. Michael Douglas commercial footage may be included only if separately cleared for this use.

broadcast program / fidelity: Do not accelerate startup or recalculation, conceal failures through misleading cuts, or present pre-recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and show only qualified claims.

broadcast program / timing: Record throughout June 5–8; begin station outreach before NCC and distribute edited packages after the conference as edits and broadcast clearances are completed. Exact delivery dates and runtime remain production decisions.

broadcast program / engineering: Qualify a custom Aurelia digital-video-to-projection/recording path; rehearse readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Use a backup demonstration system and clearly identified recorded fallback.
Post-NCC 1978 recording, editing and television distribution

message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
claim_policy: Legacy acceptance wording (not new confirmation) / status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

acceptance gates / 0: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
acceptance gates / 1: Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
acceptance gates / 2: Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, tuition, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified and separately quoted.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

broadcast policy: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The following BPI demonstration shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

stage.label: bpi
stage.description: Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in the subsequent partners section.

stage.label: partners
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: academy
stage.description: Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice, 50% tuition purchase credit and direct ordering. stage.label: packages
stage.description: State complete package contents and prices, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions.
